ELIGIBILITY
You will need to complete an application for medical coverage.
We will review the application to determine if the subscriber or dependent child is eligible for coverage.
Our decision will be based on the eligibility rules in this certificate and our underwriting policies.
If the subscriber commits fraud or intentionally lies about a material fact when filling out
the application, this coverage may be rescinded. See Page 7 for “Rescission”.
Who Is Eligible to Receive Benefits
Only pediatric members can be covered under this certificate.
Pediatric members must be:
• An independent individual who is 18 years of age or younger on the plan’s effective date and
enrolled as a subscriber in a BCBSM or BCN qualified health plan or medical plan.
The subscriber’s spouse and dependent children may also be covered under this
certificate if they are 18 years of age or younger on the plan’s effective date.
Or
• A dependent individual who is 18 years of age or younger on the plan’s effective date and is
enrolled under this certificate by a qualified health plan or medical plan subscriber. The subscriber
must be someone legally authorized to sign a contract on the dependent child’s behalf or related to
the child by:
− Birth
− Marriage
− Legal adoption
− Legal guardianship
The spouse or children of a dependent child are not covered under this certificate.
Independent and dependent pediatric members must be residents of Michigan on the effective date of
coverage and U.S. citizens or lawfully present in the United States and must intend to live in the state,
except in the case of members living outside of Michigan temporarily (as in the case with college
students or snowbirds).

To get coverage:
• Independent individuals who are 18 years of age or younger on the plan’s effective date can apply
for their own coverage by submitting their own completed application.
• For a dependent child, a parent, legal guardian or someone who is legally authorized to sign a

If the subscriber or dependent child’s BCBSM or BCN medical health plan is terminated or if the

BILLING
Information About Your Bill
Each bill for a regular billing cycle covers a one-month period.
If the subscriber purchased this coverage on the Marketplace and the Marketplace determines if the
subscriber is eligible for a federal premium tax credit (subsidy):
• The subscriber is responsible only for the subscriber’s portion of the premium, not any applicable
amount covered by the subsidy.
You may get subsidies only if this coverage was purchased on the Marketplace
• If the subscriber is receiving an advance payment of a subsidy and has paid at least one full month
of premium during the current benefit year, they will be given a three-month grace period before we
will terminate or cancel this coverage for not paying the premium when due. If a member receives
vision services at any time during the second and third months of the grace period, we will hold
payment for claims for these services beginning on the first day of the second month of the grace
period. We will notify your providers that we are not paying these claims during this time.
• If we do not receive payment in full for all premiums due before the grace period ends, this
coverage will be terminated or cancelled. The last day of coverage will be the last day of the first
month of the three-month grace period. All claims for any vision services that were provided after
that last day of coverage will be denied.
If the subscriber purchased this coverage either on or off the Marketplace but is not eligible for a subsidy:
• The subscriber is responsible for the entire premium amount.
• The subscriber must pay the premium by the due date printed on the bill. When we receive
payment, we will continue this coverage through the period that has been paid.
• The three-month grace period does not apply if the subscriber does not receive a premium tax
credit. If we do not receive premium payment by the due date, we will allow a grace period of 31
days, during which we will send a final bill. If we do not receive premium payment during the grace
period, this coverage will be terminated or cancelled as of the last day of paid coverage.
We will accept payment of your vision insurance premium only from the subscriber, or
his or her spouse, or when appropriate, from a parent, blood relative, legal guardian or
other person or entity that is allowed by law to pay premiums on your behalf.
How Rates Are Classified
The rate will be based upon certain rating factors such as age and where members live in accordance
with federal law.

CHANGING YOUR COVERAGE
The subscriber may change this coverage only during the annual open enrollment period or at other
times of the year as established by federal law.
The subscriber can change who can receive benefits under this coverage if there is a qualifying event
such as, but not limited to:
• Birth
• Adoption
• Marriage
• Divorce
• Death of a member
• Start or end of military service
Purchase on the Health Insurance Marketplace
If the subscriber purchased this coverage on the Health Insurance Marketplace (Marketplace), the
subscriber must notify the Marketplace within 60 days of any changes. The subscriber generally has up
to 60 days after the event to make a new plan selection. The date of this change is set by federal law.
Purchase off the Health Insurance Marketplace
If the subscriber purchased this coverage off the Marketplace, we must receive notice from the
subscriber within 60 days of the change. The date of the change and contract change effective dates
are set by federal law. Not all effective dates are assigned the date of the event. The effective date
depends on the type of event and options allowable by law.
If a pediatric member on the contract dies, please notify us, and the rate will be adjusted as of the date
of death. If the subscriber dies, the contract will be rewritten to reflect a new subscriber and the rate will
be adjusted. In either event, the coverage cannot be changed until the next open enrollment period,
except as established by federal law.
When the subscriber is changing this coverage, supporting proof of the change must be provided. For a
list of acceptable proofs, please visit bcbsm.com/documents.
Once the new ID card is received, do not use the old ID card. However, keep the old card until all
claims under prior vision certificate have been resolved.

TERMINATION
How to Terminate Your Coverage
We will only accept termination of this coverage from the subscriber, or for a dependent child, the
parent, guardian, or legal representative of the person(s) listed on this contract. Your coverage will be
terminated and all benefits under this certificate will end.
If the subscriber terminates this coverage and the premium is due, BCBSM reserves the right to collect
this premium from the subscriber. The subscriber may not be able to enroll in a vision product until the
next annual open enrollment or the subscriber experiences a qualifying event.
Purchase on the Health Insurance Marketplace
If the subscriber purchased coverage on the Marketplace, it may be terminated only if the subscriber
provides the Marketplace with proper notice. To terminate this coverage, the subscriber must also
terminate medical coverage under their Qualified Health Plan. The effective date of the request will be
one of the dates described in Section 5, under “Termination of Coverage”. Coverage will then be
terminated and all benefits under this certificate will end.
Purchase off the Health Insurance Marketplace
If the subscriber purchased coverage off the Marketplace, the subscriber should call or send us a
written request to terminate coverage at the phone number or address listed in Section 8, “How to
Reach VSP.” The subscriber may also call the phone number on their BCBSM identification card. The
subscriber must notify us within 30 days of the requested termination date. Coverage will then be
terminated on the requested date and all benefits under this certificate will end.
If the subscriber decides to terminate this coverage within 10 days after the date that it is
effective, the subscriber will be given a full refund of the premium that was paid as long as
no one who is covered has used benefits. If this coverage is terminated after it has been
effective for 10 days, the subscriber will be given a pro-rated refund of any unused portion
of the premium.
How We Terminate Your Coverage
Your coverage automatically ends when you are no longer eligible for coverage under this certificate.
A dependent child’s coverage automatically ends when he or she is no longer eligible for coverage
under this certificate.
In this situation, only the ineligible dependent child’s coverage will be terminated. Coverage for
eligible pediatric members who may also be on this contract will remain active.

How We Terminate Your Coverage (continued)
We will terminate your coverage if:
• The subscriber changes to a non-BCBSM medical plan.
• The subscriber does not pay the bill on time.
• The subscriber or dependent child is serving a criminal sentence for defrauding BCBSM.
• The subscriber or dependent child cannot provide proof that they are a Michigan resident, except for
individuals living outside of Michigan temporarily (as in the case with college students or snowbirds).
• We no longer offer this coverage.
• The subscriber fails to repay BCBSM for payments we made for services that were not a benefit
under this certificate, subject to the right to appeal.
• The subscriber is satisfying a civil judgment in a case involving BCBSM.
• The subscriber is repaying BCBSM funds received illegally.
• The subscriber or dependent misuses this coverage
Misuse includes illegal or improper use of your coverage such as:
− Allowing an ineligible person to use this coverage
− Requesting payment for services you did not receive
This coverage will end on the last day covered by the last premium payment. If a subscriber or
dependent child is no longer eligible for coverage because of age, coverage will end on the last day of
the calendar year in which that individual turns age 19.
If we terminate this coverage, we will provide 30 days’ notice, along with the reason for the termination.
Rescission
We will rescind coverage if the subscriber or dependent child has:
• Performed an act, practice, or omission that constitutes fraud, or
• Intentionally lied about a material fact to BCBSM or another party, which results in the subscriber or
a dependent obtaining or retaining coverage with BCBSM or the payment of claims under this or
another BCBSM certificate.
We may rescind coverage back to the effective date of the contract. If we do, we will
provide a 30-day notice. Once we notify the subscriber that we are rescinding this
coverage, we may hold or reject claims during this 30-day period. The subscriber must
repay BCBSM for its payment for any services received.

Section 3: Coverage for Vision Care Services
This section describes covered vision services we pay for and to the extent to which they are covered.
Frequency
We pay for:
• One eye exam every calendar year
• One pair of lenses or contact lenses every calendar year
• One pair of frames every calendar year
Eye Exam
We pay for an eye exam performed by an ophthalmologist or optometrist. The exam must include the
following:
• History
• Testing of visual acuity
• External exams of the eye
• Binocular measure
• Ophthalmoscopic examinations
• Tonometry (test for glaucoma) when indicated
• Medication for dilating the pupils and desensitizing the eyes for tonometry, if necessary
• Summary of findings
Lenses
We pay for standard lenses that are prescribed and dispensed by an ophthalmologist or optometrist.
• Lenses may be molded or ground, glass or plastic.
• Lenses must be equal in quality to the first-quality lens series made by American Optical, Bausch &
Lomb or Tillyer and Univis.
• The lens blank must meet Z80.1 or Z80.2 standards of the American National Standards Institute.

Guidelines to Determine Primary Coverage If You Are Covered by Two or More Plans
(1) If an individual is covered by 2 or more plans, the rules for determining the order of benefit
payments are as follows:
(a) The insurer that issues the primary plan shall pay or provide benefits as if a secondary plan
does not exist.
(b) If the individual is covered by more than 1 secondary plan, the order of benefit determination
rules under this act determine the order under which secondary plan benefits are determined in
relation to each other. An insurer that issues a secondary plan shall take into consideration the
benefits of the primary plan and the benefits of any other plan that are, under this act,
determined to be payable before those of the secondary plan.
(c) Subject to subdivision (d), a plan that does not contain order of benefit determination provisions
that are consistent with this act is always the primary plan unless the provisions of both plans,
regardless of this subdivision, state that the complying plan is primary.
(d) If the primary plan is a closed panel plan and the secondary plan is not a closed panel plan, the
insurer that issues the secondary plan shall pay or provide benefits as if it were the primary plan
if a covered person uses a nonpanel provider, except for emergency services or authorized
referrals that are paid or provided by the insurer that issued the primary plan.
Order of Benefit Payments
(2) The order in which benefits are payable by insurers that issue plans are determined by using the
first of the following rules that applies:
(a) The nondependent/dependent rule. If the individual is not a dependent but is an employee,
member, subscriber, policyholder, or retiree under 1 plan and is a dependent under another
plan, the order of payment of benefits under the plans is determined as follows:
(i) Except as otherwise provided in subparagraph (ii), the plan that covers the individual other
than as a dependent is the primary plan and the plan that covers the individual as a
dependent is the secondary plan.
(ii) If the individual is a Medicare beneficiary and, as a result of the provisions of title XVIII of the
social security act, 42 USC 1395 to 1395lll, Medicare is secondary to the plan covering the
individual as a dependent and primary to the plan covering the individual as other than a
dependent, then the order of benefits is reversed and the plan covering the individual as
other than a dependent is the secondary plan and the plan covering the individual as a
dependent is the primary plan.
(b) The dependent covered under more than 1 plan rule. If the individual is a dependent child,
unless there is a court order or judgment stating otherwise, the order of payment of benefits
under the plans covering the dependent child is determined as follows:
